description: The rose is a woody perennial flowering plant known for its beauty and fragrance.
interesting_facts: Roses have been cultivated for over 5,000 years. There are over 300 species and thousands of cultivars. The oldest fossil rose is 35 million years old.
care_instructions: Plant in full sun with well-drained soil. Water deeply once a week. Prune in late winter or early spring. Fertilize regularly during growing season.

images.alt: Wild rose (Rosa canina) in focus stacked macro shot
Rosa multiflora cluster of white blooms

description: The sunflower is a tall, annual plant with large daisy-like flower heads.
interesting_facts: Sunflowers track the sun — young flower heads face east in the morning and follow the sun west. A single sunflower head can contain up to 2,000 seeds.
care_instructions: Plant in full sun after frost danger passes. Space seeds 6 inches apart. Water regularly but avoid overwatering. Support tall varieties with stakes.

description: Lavender is a fragrant, purple-flowered shrub native to the Mediterranean.
interesting_facts: The name lavender comes from the Latin "lavare" meaning to wash — Romans used it in baths. Its scent is known for calming and relaxing properties.
care_instructions: Plant in well-drained alkaline soil in full sun. Water sparingly once established. Prune after flowering to maintain shape. Tolerates drought well.

images.alt: Lavandula multifida with divided leaves and purple blooms

description: Tulips are spring-blooming perennial bulbs with cup-shaped flowers in a wide range of colours.
interesting_facts: Tulips caused the first economic bubble — "Tulip Mania" in the 1630s saw single bulbs sell for more than 10 times a skilled worker's annual income.
care_instructions: Plant bulbs in autumn, 4–6 inches deep in well-drained soil. Full sun to partial shade. Remove spent flowers but leave foliage to die back naturally.

images.alt: Red and white tulip at Myddelton House, Enfield

description: The common daisy is a cheerful perennial with white petals around a yellow centre.
interesting_facts: Daisies are actually two flowers in one — the white petals are ray florets and the yellow centre is made of disc florets. The name comes from "day's eye" because they open at dawn.
care_instructions: Grows in most soil types in full sun to partial shade. Water moderately. Deadhead spent flowers to encourage continuous blooming. Divide clumps every 2–3 years.

images.alt: Bellis perennis full plant in bloom

description: Orchids are a diverse family of flowering plants known for their intricate and exotic blooms.
interesting_facts: Orchids are one of the largest plant families with over 28,000 species. Some orchids can live over 100 years. Vanilla flavour comes from an orchid species.
care_instructions: Bright indirect light. Water weekly allowing roots to dry between waterings. Use specialised orchid bark mix. Maintain humidity above 50%. Fertilise weakly weekly.

images.alt: Phalaenopsis orchid cultivar with white blooms

description: Cherry blossoms are delicate pink flowers that bloom on ornamental cherry trees in early spring.
interesting_facts: Cherry blossom season in Japan is celebrated with "hanami" — the tradition of flower viewing. The blossoms only last 1–2 weeks, symbolising the fleeting nature of life.
care_instructions: Plant in full sun with well-drained loamy soil. Water deeply during dry spells. Prune in late summer to avoid disease. Protect from strong winds.

images.alt: Prunus serrulata branch with pink blossoms
Cherry tree (Prunus serrulata) in full bloom

description: Hydrangeas are deciduous shrubs known for their large, showy flower clusters that change colour based on soil pH.
interesting_facts: Hydrangea flower colour is determined by soil pH — acidic soil produces blue flowers, alkaline soil produces pink. They contain a compound called hydrangin that is toxic if ingested.
care_instructions: Plant in morning sun with afternoon shade. Keep soil consistently moist. Prune after flowering. Add aluminium sulphate for blue flowers or lime for pink.

images.alt: Pink and blue hydrangea flower clusters

description: The lily is a tall perennial herb with large, prominent trumpet-shaped flowers and a sweet fragrance.
interesting_facts: Lilies have been cultivated for over 3,000 years. In Christian symbolism, the Madonna lily represents purity. Some lily bulbs are edible and were used as food by ancient civilisations.
care_instructions: Plant bulbs in well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade. Water regularly during growth. Stake tall varieties. Remove spent flowers but leave stems to die back naturally.

images.alt: Orange Lilium bulbiferum flower in bloom

description: Daffodils are spring-blooming bulbs with bright yellow trumpet-shaped flowers surrounded by a star-shaped collar of petals.
interesting_facts: Daffodils are the national flower of Wales. The name Narcissus comes from the Greek myth of a youth who fell in love with his own reflection. All parts of the plant are toxic due to lycorine.
care_instructions: Plant bulbs in autumn, 3–4 inches deep in well-drained soil. Full sun to partial shade. Allow foliage to die back naturally after flowering. Divide clumps every 3–5 years.

images.alt: Cluster of yellow daffodils in bloom

description: Peonies are herbaceous perennials with large, showy, often fragrant flowers in shades of pink, red, white, and yellow.
interesting_facts: Peonies are known as the 'king of flowers' in China, where they have been cultivated for over 2,000 years. They can live for over 100 years and are often planted as heirloom specimens.
care_instructions: Plant in full sun with rich, well-drained soil. Position crowns no more than 2 inches deep. Water deeply during dry spells. Provide support for heavy blooms. Cut back foliage in autumn.

images.alt: Pink peony flower in full bloom

description: Irises are perennial plants with striking, intricate flowers featuring three upright petals and three drooping sepals.
interesting_facts: The iris is named after the Greek goddess of the rainbow. It has been the fleur-de-lis symbol of French royalty for centuries. There are over 300 species in the genus.
care_instructions: Plant rhizomes in full sun with well-drained soil. Ensure rhizomes are partially exposed above soil. Water moderately. Divide every 3–4 years after flowering to maintain vigour.

description: Chrysanthemums are flowering perennials known for their dense, showy flower heads in a wide range of colours and forms.
interesting_facts: Chrysanthemums are the national flower of Japan and the symbol of the Japanese imperial family. They naturally bloom in autumn, making them the quintessential fall flower.
care_instructions: Plant in full sun with rich, well-drained soil. Pinch back stems in spring for bushier growth. Water at base to avoid foliar diseases. Protect from frost. Divide every 2–3 years.

description: Marigolds are cheerful annuals with bright orange, yellow, and red pom-pom flower heads.
interesting_facts: Marigolds are known as the 'herb of the sun' and are used in Day of the Dead celebrations in Mexico. Their roots release compounds that repel nematodes in the soil.
care_instructions: Plant in full sun after frost danger passes. Water at soil level to prevent powdery mildew. Deadhead spent blooms regularly. Tolerates poor soil but thrives in well-drained conditions.

description: Dahlias are tuberous perennials that produce spectacular geometric flower heads in nearly every colour except blue.
interesting_facts: Dahlias were first cultivated by the Aztecs as a food source. The tubers were eaten like potatoes. There are over 50,000 registered dahlia cultivars worldwide.
care_instructions: Plant tubers in spring after frost, in full sun with rich well-drained soil. Water deeply 2–3 times per week. Stake tall varieties. Deadhead regularly. Dig up tubers before first frost in cold climates.

description: Gerberas are striking daisy-like flowers with large, colourful heads on long, sturdy stems.
interesting_facts: Gerbera daisies are the fifth most popular cut flower in the world. They are known for their ability to absorb pollutants from the air. Each flower head is actually hundreds of tiny individual flowers.
care_instructions: Plant in full sun with well-drained soil. Water at base to prevent crown rot. Deadhead spent blooms. Protect from heavy frost. Divide every 2–3 years.

description: Zinnias are vibrant annuals with solitary daisy-like flower heads in a rainbow of bright colours.
interesting_facts: Zinnias are one of the easiest flowers to grow from seed. They are named after German botanist Johann Gottfried Zinn. The flowers are edible and attract butterflies and hummingbirds.
care_instructions: Sow seeds directly in full sun after frost. Water at soil level. Deadhead spent blooms for continuous flowering. Space plants well for good air circulation. Resistant to most pests.

description: Carnations are herbaceous perennials with frilled, multi-petalled flowers that are among the most popular cut flowers worldwide.
interesting_facts: Carnations symbolise love and fascination. The pink carnation is the official Mother's Day flower. They are one of the few flowers that can be naturally coloured in shades of green, blue, and purple through dyeing.
care_instructions: Plant in full sun with alkaline, well-drained soil. Pinch back young plants for bushier growth. Water moderately. Support tall varieties. Deadhead spent blooms to prolong flowering.

description: Hibiscus is a tropical shrub with large, showy trumpet-shaped flowers that come in a wide range of vibrant colours.
interesting_facts: Hibiscus is the national flower of Malaysia, Haiti, and South Korea. The flowers are used to make a popular herbal tea rich in vitamin C. Each bloom only lasts one day.
care_instructions: Plant in full sun with rich, well-drained soil. Water generously during growing season. Prune in early spring to shape. Protect from temperatures below 10°C. Fertilise monthly during bloom.

images.alt: Red hibiscus flower with prominent stamen

description: The common poppy is an annual herb with delicate, papery red petals and a distinctive dark centre.
interesting_facts: Poppies are emblematic of remembrance for fallen soldiers, inspired by the WWI poem 'In Flanders Fields'. Each poppy flower contains up to 40,000 seeds. The seeds can remain dormant for over 80 years.
care_instructions: Sow seeds directly in full sun in spring or autumn. Thrives in poor, well-drained soil. Water sparingly. Self-seeds readily. Deadhead to prevent unwanted spreading.

description: Violets are small, delicate perennials with heart-shaped leaves and fragrant purple, blue, or white flowers.
interesting_facts: Violets were the favourite flower of Napoleon Bonaparte and were used as a symbol by his supporters. The flowers can be candied and used in desserts. Viola tricolor is the wild pansy.
care_instructions: Plant in partial to full shade with moist, well-drained soil. Water regularly. Remove spent flowers. Mulch to retain moisture. Divide clumps in autumn every 2–3 years.

description: Petunias are popular annuals with trumpet-shaped flowers that bloom profusely in a wide range of colours and patterns.
interesting_facts: Petunias are related to tomatoes, potatoes, and tobacco. They are one of the most popular bedding plants in the world. Some varieties are fragrant at night to attract nocturnal moths.
care_instructions: Plant in full sun with well-drained soil. Water regularly, especially in containers. Pinch back stems to encourage bushiness. Fertilise every two weeks. Remove spent flowers for continuous bloom.

description: Hyacinths are spring-blooming bulbs that produce dense spikes of highly fragrant bell-shaped flowers.
interesting_facts: In Greek myth, hyacinths sprang from the blood of the youth Hyacinthus. Hyacinth bulbs contain oxalic acid and can cause skin irritation. Their intense fragrance can fill an entire room.
care_instructions: Plant bulbs in autumn, 4–6 inches deep in well-drained soil. Full sun to partial shade. Water during active growth. After flowering, allow foliage to die back naturally. Bulbs may need replacing after 3–4 years.

description: Gardenias are evergreen shrubs with creamy-white, waxy flowers that are renowned for their intoxicating fragrance.
interesting_facts: Gardenias are named after Dr Alexander Garden, a Scottish naturalist. The flowers are used in perfumery and as a flavouring in tea. They symbolise secret love and joy.
care_instructions: Plant in partial shade with acidic, well-drained soil. Keep soil consistently moist. Mist leaves regularly. Fertilise with acid-loving plant food. Prune after flowering.

description: Azaleas are flowering shrubs that produce masses of bright trumpet-shaped flowers in spring, often covering the entire plant.
interesting_facts: Azaleas are part of the Rhododendron genus. Some species are toxic—honey made from azalea nectar can cause 'mad honey' poisoning. They are the national flower of Nepal.
care_instructions: Plant in partial shade with acidic, well-drained soil. Keep soil moist with organic mulch. Avoid deep planting. Fertilise after flowering. Prune lightly to shape.

images.alt: Pink azalea flowers in full bloom

description: Magnolias are ancient flowering trees or shrubs with large, fragrant cup-shaped flowers in white, pink, or purple.
interesting_facts: Magnolies are among the oldest flowering plants, with fossils dating back 95 million years. They evolved before bees and were originally pollinated by beetles. The magnolia is the state flower of Mississippi and Louisiana.
care_instructions: Plant in full sun to partial shade with deep, rich, well-drained soil. Water deeply during dry spells. Mulch generously. Prune minimally after flowering. Protect from strong winds.

description: Frangipani is a tropical tree or shrub with clusters of highly fragrant, five-petalled flowers in shades of pink, white, yellow, and red.
interesting_facts: The frangipani is the national flower of Laos and is associated with temples in Bali and Thailand. Despite its tropical appearance, it stores water in its thick succulent branches and tolerates drought well.
care_instructions: Plant in full sun with sharp-draining sandy soil. Water sparingly—allow soil to dry between waterings. Fertilise during growing season. Protect from frost. Prune in winter dormancy.

description: Peace lilies are popular indoor plants with elegant white spathes (modified leaves) that resemble flags of peace.
interesting_facts: Peace lilies are excellent air purifiers, removing VOCs like benzene and formaldehyde. Despite the name, they are not true lilies. The white 'petal' is actually a modified leaf called a spathe.
care_instructions: Thrives in low to bright indirect light. Water when soil is dry to the touch. Mist leaves regularly. Fertilise monthly during growing season. Repot when root-bound. Tolerates neglect well.

images.alt: Peace lily plant with white spathe

description: Snapdragons are tall, colourful perennials with unique dragon-head-shaped flowers that open and close like a mouth when squeezed.
interesting_facts: The name comes from the flower's resemblance to a dragon's mouth. Squeezing the sides causes the 'mouth' to open. Snapdragons are a symbol of grace and strength.
care_instructions: Plant in full sun with well-drained soil. Water at base to prevent fungal diseases. Deadhead spent blooms to prolong flowering. Pinch back young plants for bushier growth.

description: Begonias are popular flowering plants with waxy leaves and clusters of small, colourful blooms that flower continuously.
interesting_facts: There are over 2,000 species of begonia. They are named after Michel Bégon, a 17th-century French governor of Haiti. Some species have edible flowers with a citrus flavour.
care_instructions: Plant in partial shade with rich, well-drained soil. Water when soil feels dry. Avoid wetting foliage to prevent powdery mildew. Fertilise monthly during growing season.

description: Freesias are fragrant, funnel-shaped flowers that grow on delicate arching stems in a rainbow of colours.
interesting_facts: Freesias are among the most fragrant flowers and are widely used in perfumery. Their scent is described as honey-like with citrus notes. They symbolise friendship and innocence.
care_instructions: Plant corms in full sun with well-drained soil. Water moderately during growth. Support stems with stakes. Allow foliage to die back after flowering. Lift corms in cold climates.

description: Wisteria is a woody climbing vine that produces cascading clusters of fragrant, pea-like flowers in shades of purple, blue, pink, and white.
interesting_facts: Wisteria can live for over 100 years. The oldest known wisteria in Japan spans nearly half a hectare. All parts of the plant contain toxic compounds called wisterin and lectin.
care_instructions: Plant in full sun with rich, well-drained soil. Provide strong support structure. Prune twice yearly — in summer and winter. Water deeply during dry spells. May take years to flower.

description: Camellias are evergreen shrubs with elegant, rose-like flowers in shades of pink, red, and white that bloom in the cooler months.
interesting_facts: Camellia leaves are used to make tea. The flower is the state symbol of Alabama. In Japan, camellias represent divine love and are called tsubaki.
care_instructions: Plant in partial shade with acidic, well-drained soil. Mulch with pine bark or leaves. Water deeply during dry spells. Prune after flowering. Protect from harsh afternoon sun.

description: Anemones are delicate, poppy-like flowers with cup-shaped petals in vivid shades of red, blue, purple, and white surrounding a dark centre.
interesting_facts: The name anemone comes from the Greek word for wind, earning them the nickname windflower. In Greek myth, they sprang from the tears of Aphrodite mourning Adonis.
care_instructions: Plant tubers in autumn in well-drained soil. Full sun to partial shade. Water regularly during growth. Soak tubers overnight before planting. Mulch for winter protection.

description: Delphiniums are stately perennials with tall spikes of densely packed, spurred flowers in shades of blue, purple, pink, and white.
interesting_facts: The name comes from the Latin for dolphin, referring to the shape of the flower buds. All parts of the plant are highly toxic if ingested. Delphinium flowers were used by Native Americans for blue dye.
care_instructions: Plant in full sun with rich, alkaline, well-drained soil. Stake tall flower spikes. Water at base regularly. Cut back after first bloom for second flowering. Divide every 2–3 years.

description: Foxgloves are tall, elegant biennials with tubular, bell-shaped flowers that grow along one side of a towering spike.
interesting_facts: Foxglove is the source of the heart medication digitalis, used to treat cardiac conditions. The name comes from folklore that foxes wore the flowers as gloves so as not to disturb the hens.
care_instructions: Plant in partial shade with rich, acidic, well-drained soil. Water regularly. Remove spent flower spikes to encourage second bloom. Self-seeds readily. All parts are toxic so handle with gloves.

description: Honeysuckle is a twining climbing vine with highly fragrant, trumpet-shaped flowers that open cream and fade to yellow or pink.
interesting_facts: Honeysuckle nectar is edible and sweet — children often suck the flowers for a drop of honey. The scent is strongest in the evening to attract night-flying moths. In folklore, honeysuckle brings dreams of love.
care_instructions: Plant in full sun to partial shade with well-drained soil. Provide support for climbing. Water deeply during dry spells. Prune after flowering to control growth. Mulch roots to keep cool.

description: Jasmine is a fragrant flowering shrub or vine with small, star-shaped white or yellow flowers known for their sweet, intoxicating scent.
interesting_facts: Jasmine is known as the queen of the night because its flowers release their strongest fragrance after sunset. It is the national flower of Pakistan, Indonesia, and the Philippines. Jasmine oil is a key ingredient in many perfumes.
care_instructions: Plant in full sun to partial shade with well-drained soil. Water regularly during growth. Prune after flowering. Provide support for climbing varieties. Fertilise monthly during growing season.

description: Lilacs are deciduous shrubs that produce large, cone-shaped clusters of highly fragrant, tubular flowers in shades of purple, pink, and white.
interesting_facts: Lilacs are associated with the Greek myth of the nymph Syringa. The scent of lilac is said to have calming properties and is used in aromatherapy. A lilac tree can live up to 200 years.
care_instructions: Plant in full sun with alkaline, well-drained soil. Water deeply during dry spells. Prune immediately after flowering. Remove suckers to control spread. Fertilise lightly in early spring.

description: Oleander is a tough evergreen shrub with clusters of showy, five-petalled flowers in pink, red, white, and yellow that bloom throughout the warm months.
interesting_facts: Oleander is one of the most poisonous ornamental plants — all parts contain cardiac glycosides. Despite its toxicity, it is widely planted along highways for its drought tolerance. It is the national flower of Hiroshima.
care_instructions: Plant in full sun with well-drained soil. Extremely drought-tolerant once established. Water sparingly. Prune in autumn to shape. Protect from frost in colder climates. Wear gloves when handling.

description: Pansies are cheerful, low-growing plants with distinctive face-like markings on their five-petalled flowers in a vast array of colours.
interesting_facts: The name pansy comes from the French pensee meaning thought. In Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream, pansy juice was used as a love potion. They are edible flowers with a mild, sweet flavour.
care_instructions: Plant in full sun to partial shade with rich, well-drained soil. Water regularly. Deadhead spent blooms to encourage continuous flowering. Fertilise every two weeks. Mulch to keep roots cool.

description: Salvias are striking perennials with tall spikes of vibrant red, purple, or blue tubular flowers that are magnets for pollinators.
interesting_facts: The name comes from the Latin salvare meaning to heal — many salvias have medicinal properties. Sage (Salvia officinalis) is a culinary relative. Salvia flowers produce nectar that attracts hummingbirds and butterflies.
care_instructions: Plant in full sun with well-drained soil. Water regularly but avoid overhead watering. Deadhead spent spikes. Cut back hard in early spring. Divide every 3–4 years. Tolerates heat and humidity well.

description: Snowdrops are delicate, early-blooming bulbs with drooping white bell-shaped flowers that often emerge through snow.
interesting_facts: Snowdrops are one of the first flowers to bloom in late winter, symbolising hope and the promise of spring. The flower contains galantamine, used to treat Alzheimer's disease. They naturalise readily in lawns.
care_instructions: Plant bulbs in autumn, 2–3 inches deep in well-drained soil. Partial shade preferred. Allow foliage to die back naturally after flowering. Divide clumps after flowering every 3–5 years.

description: Sweet peas are climbing annuals with highly fragrant, butterfly-shaped flowers in soft pastel shades of pink, purple, blue, and white.
interesting_facts: Sweet peas are one of the most fragrant garden flowers. Their scent is best in the morning. The flowers are edible but the seeds and pods are toxic if eaten in quantity. They are a symbol of blissful pleasure.
care_instructions: Sow seeds in early spring in full sun with rich, well-drained soil. Provide supports for climbing. Water regularly at soil level. Deadhead spent blooms for continuous flowering. Pick flowers frequently to encourage more blooms.

images.alt: Pink sweet pea flowers on vine

description: Thistles are robust biennials with spiny leaves and spherical purple or pink flower heads that are beloved by bees and butterflies.
interesting_facts: The thistle is the national emblem of Scotland. Despite their prickly reputation, thistle flowers produce abundant nectar. The fluffy seed heads (pappus) can disperse seeds over long distances by wind.
care_instructions: Thrives in poor, well-drained soil in full sun. Tolerates drought once established. Self-seeds freely. Remove flower heads before seed set to control spread. Minimal care required.

description: Verbena is a tall, airy perennial with clusters of small purple flowers held on slender, branching stems above sparse foliage.
interesting_facts: Verbena has been used in herbal medicine for centuries. The ancient Romans used it in ceremonies and it was called the holy herb. It is extremely attractive to butterflies and pollinators.
care_instructions: Plant in full sun with well-drained soil. Water moderately once established. Cut back in late winter to promote vigorous growth. Self-seeds readily. Tolerates heat, humidity, and drought well.

images.alt: Purple verbena flowers on tall stems

description: Yarrow is a hardy perennial with flat-topped clusters of tiny flowers in white, pink, yellow, or red above feathery, aromatic foliage.
interesting_facts: Yarrow is named after the Greek hero Achilles, who used it to treat wounds on the battlefield. Its feathery leaves give it the species name millefolium meaning thousand leaves. It is a valuable medicinal herb.
care_instructions: Plant in full sun with well-drained soil. Extremely drought-tolerant. Cut back after flowering for a second bloom. Divide clumps every 2–3 years. Deadhead to prevent excessive self-seeding.

description: Bleeding hearts are shade-loving perennials with arching stems of distinctive heart-shaped pink flowers that appear to drip with a white teardrop.
interesting_facts: Each flower resembles a heart with a droplet, giving the plant its romantic name. In Victorian flower language, bleeding hearts symbolise passionate love. Despite their delicate appearance, they are extremely cold-hardy.
care_instructions: Plant in partial to full shade with rich, moist, well-drained soil. Water regularly. Mulch to keep roots cool and moist. Cut back yellowing foliage after flowering. Divide in early spring every 3–5 years.

images.alt: Pink bleeding heart flowers on arching stem
